rows.text: Ankit Chand is a Data Scientist, Generative AI Engineer, and Agentic AI Developer based in India. He has nearly three years of industry experience in data science, focusing on entity extraction for e-commerce search and GCP model pipelines. Since mid-2024, he has worked on designing multi-agent LLM systems using Python, FastAPI, Microsoft AutoGen, and Azure OpenAI. He builds predictable, deterministic, and honest AI systems. [1]

Ankit is a data scientist specializing in generative AI and agentic systems. He has worked on time-series forecasting and developed machine learning models in industry, including a Conditional Random Field model at Retisio. Since mid-2024, he has focused on LLM systems, working with retrieval-augmented question answering and multi-agent platforms like NexusAI and IntelliHub [3]. He is currently a Data Science Intern pursuing a postgraduate program in Data Science with Generative AI [2].

Ankit's current technical specialization is Generative AI and Agentic AI, as he is self-directed, full-time specializing in these areas [4]. He has built multi-agent LLM systems using Python, FastAPI, Microsoft AutoGen, and Azure OpenAI, with focus on orchestration, ReAct tool calling, intent routing, and streaming APIs. His work includes automated test suites to ensure reliability [4].

Ankit is currently a Data Science Intern at Unified Mentor Private Limited, working on time-series forecasting [2]. He is also pursuing a PG Program in Data Science with Generative AI through Great Learning [1].

- Built time-series forecasts with SARIMA, ETS, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting models [2]  
- Halved the 4-week forecast error against the baseline [2]

Ankit has worked with a variety of machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SARIMA/ETS for time series forecasting. He also used Gradient Boosting and Deep Learning techniques like CNN and RNN. These algorithms were applied in projects such as Telecom Churn Prediction, UAC Care Load & Placement Forecasting, and Lead Scoring for an Online Education Company [2].

Ankit has experience with XGBoost, as evidenced by his use of XGBoost in the A Fine Windy Day — Wind Power Prediction project [1]. In this project, he compared various regression models, including XGBoost and LightGBM, to build a predictive model for wind power. The project utilized XGBoost as part of a blended model for the final submission [3].

Ankit has applied feature engineering in multiple projects, including the Search Intelligence Tool (SIT) at Retisio India Pvt. Ltd., where he built a CRF model for entity recognition. He used feature engineering to prepare data for the model, including noise reduction and spell-checking. In the Telecom Churn Prediction project, he applied feature engineering to enhance model performance. His experience includes using Python, Pandas, and Scikit-learn for data preprocessing and feature selection [3].

Ankit's approach to model evaluation involves comparing multiple models (SARIMA, ETS, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) against a baseline using 4-week-ahead error metrics. He evaluates model performance by reducing error relative to the baseline, selecting the approach that halved the error. This is done through statistical analysis and systematic comparison, ensuring robust and reliable model selection [2][3].

Ankit applied time-series forecasting techniques like SARIMA and ETS in UAC Care Load & Placement Forecasting to predict care load and placement. He used Python, Pandas, and machine learning models to prepare data, fit models, and evaluate performance. The system compared models' 4-week error against a baseline, selecting the approach that halved the error. The code is not public, but a walkthrough is available on request. [1][2][3][4]

Ankit has implemented several Generative AI projects, including NexusAI, IntelliHub, Teachable AI for Structured Metadata Extraction, RAG-Powered QA for Medical Research, and Autonomous Code Generation & Execution. Each project uses AutoGen agents, tools, and frameworks like Flask, PyPDF2, FAISS, and LangChain. The projects leverage deterministic intent classification, concurrent execution, and model grounding to achieve efficient and accurate results [1][2][3][4][5].

Ankit has experience with RAG, as demonstrated by his implementation of a RAG-Powered QA for Medical Research system [1]. He used RAG in a pipeline that included source retrieval, text extraction, embedding, indexing, similarity search, and generation [2]. The system uses Python, LangChain, OpenAI embeddings, and FAISS, and is deployed as a REST API [3]. The system's key features include question answering grounded in research papers and paper summarisation [4]. 

- RAG is used for question answering grounded in research papers.  
- The system uses FAISS for fast vector similarity search.  
- The code is not public, but a walkthrough is available on request.  
- Ankit's role was Developer.

Ankit has used Large Language Models (GPT-4o, GPT-4) and frameworks like LangChain, Azure OpenAI, and OpenAI API in various projects. He has also utilized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and vector databases (FAISS, ChromaDB) in his work. Additionally, he has applied LLM testing with mock clients and performed model evaluation using data science techniques. [1][2][3][5]

Ankit implements embeddings and vector search using OpenAI embeddings for document vectorization and FAISS for fast similarity search in the RAG-Powered QA for Medical Research project. He extracts text from PDFs, generates embeddings with the OpenAI API, indexes them in FAISS for efficient retrieval, and uses the vector database to find relevant passages for answering questions [1][3][4].

Ankit's multi-agent architecture is designed to handle complex tasks by breaking them into sub-tasks, each handled by specialized agents. The architecture includes an autonomous code generation & execution pipeline, a teachable AI for metadata extraction, a NexusAI system with a seven-stage pipeline, a search intelligence tool, and an IntelliHub system. The agents work collaboratively, with orchestration, routing, and tool calling ensuring efficient task execution. The architecture includes guardrails for safety, memory for context, and testing for reliability. The code is not public, but the project page details the architecture [1][2][3][4][5].

Ankit has used Microsoft AutoGen (Agentic AI) in IntelliHub, Teachable AI for Structured Metadata Extraction and Autonomous Code Generation & Execution. [1]

- Ankit has about 2 years 8 months of full-time industry data-science experience (nearly three years): Data Scientist at Retisio India Pvt. Ltd. (Sep 2022 – May 2024) and Data Scientist at AIE Software India Pvt. Ltd. (Sep 2021 – Sep… [2]
- Autonomous Code Generation & Execution uses Python, Microsoft AutoGen, OpenAI GPT-4o, Python virtual environment. [3]
- Autonomous Code Generation & Execution (Independent, 2024 – 2025) — Two AutoGen agents — one writes code, one runs it — iterating until the task works. [4]

Ankit orchestrates multiple AI agents using a custom Python orchestration engine in NexusAI, with a seven-stage pipeline that includes input guardrails, routing, clarification, concurrent fan-out, aggregation, output rails, and a single-writer memory commit. The system uses a hybrid router with keyword rules, context, and a GPT-4o classifier to route queries efficiently. The MasterOrchestrator sends each turn to one or more agents, and each agent uses a ReAct tool-calling loop over 31 tools. The agents collaborate with routing, guardrails, and memory management to ensure proper execution and output [4].

IntelliHub tests agents without API keys by implementing a deterministic mock that replaces the model, allowing the real agent and tool loop to run without tokens. The mock follows the real client interface, and the factory returns either the live client or the mock based on configuration, ensuring production code paths remain unchanged. Tests force offline mode, and the mock requests tools on the first turn, then writes a narrative on the second. The mock does not expose full tool results to the model, ensuring testability [1].

NexusAI is an agentic AI system developed by Ankit, featuring eight GPT-4o specialist agents that handle different tasks. It uses a MasterOrchestrator to route conversations and combine specialist answers. The system is built with Python, asyncio, and other tools, with a focus on reliability and security. The code is not public, but a walkthrough is available on request. [1]

NexusAI is thoroughly tested with 214 offline tests passing and 214 automated tests passing fully offline. A fake LLM client allows the entire suite to run without spending tokens, and all network calls go through one seam, enabling a single fixture to test every tool's fallback path [1]. The code is not public, but a walkthrough is available on request.

Ankit's most interesting AI projects include NexusAI, IntelliHub, and RAG-Powered QA for Medical Research. NexusAI features eight specialist agents and a chat interface, while IntelliHub uses Python and AI automation with a focus on structured data. RAG-Powered QA leverages a library of research PDFs for grounded answers. The code for NexusAI and IntelliHub is private, but Ankit is open to demos. [1][4]

IntelliHub's architecture is designed to handle complex queries by first determining the intent using a deterministic classifier, then selecting appropriate agents and strategies. It uses a ReAct-style planner to build an execution plan, with collectors running concurrently and a health pipeline ensuring consistency. The architecture is built with Python, asyncio, and Microsoft AutoGen, and is not publicly available. [1]

Ankit's GitHub projects include NexusAI, IntelliHub, and Gesture Recognition for Smart TVs, with the code for NexusAI and IntelliHub being public. The code for Gesture Recognition for Smart TVs is also public on GitHub. The projects are organized into categories like Deep Learning, NLP, and Agentic AI. For more details, visit the project page or contact Ankit. [1][2][3][4]
